metadata.title: Bitcoin's Next Move Depends On One Fed Decision
metadata.speaker: Jordy Visser (guest), interviewed by Anthony Pompliano

executive_takeaway: The highest-signal ideas: (1) A real deleveraging / 'fireworks show is over' is underway in AI names — the 'AI midcycle slowdown' is a second-derivative deceleration, not a thesis break. (2) Jordy is rotating hard toward crypto (Bitcoin + Ethereum + MicroStrategy) and back into memory semis (Micron), arguing crypto is the only asset with a moat AI cannot disrupt. (3) Memory is named the single most important part of the AI trade; he is focused on names that have not yet seen their earnings 'step-up function.' (4) Cooling inflation + a Warsh-led Fed reform is read as a major positive for the 'debasement trade' / crypto into year-end. (5) Open-source Chinese models (Kimi K3) are seen as NOT displacing US frontier models inside the Fortune 500 due to tooling, bureaucracy, and 'cultural weights.' (6) He expects the next leg to be 'embodied AI' / robotics, played via the semiconductor/infrastructure trade.

ai_workflows.name: Model router for cost-efficient inference
ai_workflows.goal: Answer each query with the cheapest model that is good enough
ai_workflows.tools: Sylvia product (multi-model router); high-intelligence + lower-cost/open models
ai_workflows.approach: Route complex queries to the most powerful (expensive) model; route simple queries (e.g. 'what is the date') to lower-compute/open-source models. Question still tested: how many models to include (2-3 vs 20; cite Brett Taylor's Sierra using ~20 models).
ai_workflows.why: Positive impact seen on cost/throughput; Jevons paradox — cheaper intelligence raises total usage

ai_workflows.name: Earnings 'step-up function' screen (Jordy's method)
ai_workflows.goal: Separate AI names that will keep beating earnings hard from those that won't
ai_workflows.tools: His '100 name AI portfolio'; tracks which names have vs haven't seen their earnings step-up
ai_workflows.approach: Focus on companies that have NOT yet seen their earnings step-up function and are still expected to beat by a significant amount in coming quarters (not just this quarter). Names beating by only a little (like post-2024 Nvidia) produce ~25%/yr but not 60-70x re-ratings.
ai_workflows.why: Identifies the next outperformers as the 'fireworks' phase ends

ai_workflows.name: V-adjusted position sizing
ai_workflows.goal: Size positions by volatility rather than price
ai_workflows.approach: Compare V of assets (AI thematic V ~100 vs Bitcoin V ~30) => can hold ~3x as much BTC on a V-adjusted basis. When vol rises, quant/risk-par strategies must cut risk and rebuilt positions are smaller.
ai_workflows.why: Explains the deleveraging mechanics and why crypto is comparatively attractive

risks: Speaker explicitly says deleveraging is 'real' and about leverage — a momentum unwind in tech factor was 'unprecedented.'
He warns the 'fireworks show is over': future returns are stock-specific, not broad 3-10x moves.
Contradiction/evolution: he is rebuilding a Micron position at HIGHER average prices than where he sold — acknowledges paying more.
Inflation call is his read; he notes PCE core is the one measure still pointing up — 'inflation is a non-story' is his lean, not fact.
Warsh/Fed reform thesis assumes a dovish-leaning, AI-literate Fed; July hike odds ~10% but not zero.
Assumption that US frontier models keep enterprise dominance ignores rapid open-source improvement (Kimi K3 cited as matching/beating closed models on benchmarks).
'Cultural weights' in open models is flagged as under-researched — uncertainty, not established fact.
AGI ~2030 and 'all companies disrupted' is presented as a framework, sourced to Demis Hassabis, not the speaker's own forecast.
ROIC shifting to private companies as agents accelerate is a thesis, not yet in reported data (he cites 40 S&P names reported, 16% beat).
Missing: no specific price targets, position sizes beyond 'small,' or dated entries; crypto basket constituents beyond PayPal/Robinhood/MSTR not named.
Several claims (memory bottleneck, token-exponential demand) are speaker convictions — verify with supply/capacity data independently.
